messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: p99 latency breach detected for canary service 'text-gen-canary' (v13). Alerts crossed threshold: p99 > 1.5s for 3m. Stream stalls observed. Please ack.

ingrid: acked. on-call here, looking. seeing p95 at ~650ms, p99 at 2.1s. streaming stall errors increasing.

jamie: noticed this started ~2m after the v13 traffic shift. Canary got ~15% traffic at 2026-03-15T03:12:xxZ.

chris: popping in — correlating logs now. I see a spike of kv cache miss rate and 'kv-evict: lock-wait' entries around the same time.

lina: can you paste a sample of the logs? I want to see if it's hot-keyed.

chris: sure — relevant snippet:```
[03:12:09] kv-cache evict queue length=128
[03:12:10] kvlock: wait=420ms shard=12
[03:12:11] stream: stall detected session=abcd1234 tail-latency=1800ms
[03:12:11] model:v13 generate: step 7 -> kernel OOM? fallback OK
```

devendra: interesting — the kernel OOM line looks like the runtime tried an optimized kernel and degraded. But fallback would still add latency. Might be quant/tiling difference for v13.

ingrid: what's customer impact? any 5xx increase?

jamie: 5xx are steady at baseline. This is mostly increased user-level latency and streaming stalls (clients seeing slow initial tokens). A few sessions hit >3s and dropped. Customer-impact panel: @alex can you pull top-5 customers affected in the last 15m?

alex: running query...```sql
SELECT customer, count(*) AS slow_reqs FROM request_events
WHERE service='text-gen-canary' AND latency>1500
AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY customer ORDER BY slow_reqs DESC LIMIT 5;
```

alex: results: cust-omega: 48, cust-sparrow: 12, cust-invite: 7, cust-internal-tools: 4, cust-devhub: 3. No obvious high-volume external SLA customers yet.

lina: thanks. ops risk low for revenue but still want quick mitigation. Options: 1) rollback canary to v12, 2) reduce canary traffic to 2%, 3) apply runtime kernel fallback config (force no-optimized kernels for v13). Thoughts?

chris: I can try reducing traffic first — quicker and lower blast radius. If that doesn't stabilize in 2m, we rollback.

devendra: reducing traffic will reduce the steady-state load on kv cache. But if v13 has a higher per-request memory pattern, even a small % could still expose issues. I'd prefer rollback sooner rather than risk more stalls.

ingrid: okay change proposal: reduce to 2% now, monitor 2m, then rollback if p99 > 900ms. jamie, can you handle the traffic change?

jamie: on it. running: `redwood deploy traffic shift --service text-gen-canary --from v13 --to v12 --percent 13->2 --no-wait`

ops-bot: Deploy change accepted: traffic-shift job 78ab queued. ETA ~45s.

chris: checking metrics panel: kv lock-wait and stream stalls trending down immediately. p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 1.1s within 60s. p95 stable ~600ms.

ingrid: good sign. keep watching. if p99 hits <900ms in next 3m we can avoid rollback.

jamie: traffic-shift job completed. Canary traffic now at 2%.

alex: customer impact list updated: cust-omega slow_reqs now 10 (was 48).

devendra: still seeing occasional 1.2s tail event. Might be a few stickier sessions with pinned KV shards. We should clear KV hotspots proactively: run `kvcache evict-shards --shard-list 12,18`

chris: running that now. Output:```
evict-shards: started shards=[12,18]
evict-shards: success shard=12
evict-shards: success shard=18
```

lina: p99 now 760ms, p95 580ms. streaming stalls largely gone.

ingrid: nice. can we keep canary at 2% for the next 30m and run a focused eval on v13 tokenization and tiling? devendra, can your team produce a short reproduce with pinned kv cache?

devendra: yes I'll schedule a micro-run in the lab at reduced scale and enable verbose runtime tracing for v13. Will report within 2 hours.

jamie: ops note — opened incident ticket INC-2026-0445 and set priority P2. Assigning to eng-runtime for root-cause.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0445 created by ingrid. Severity P2. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0445

ingrid: follow-ups: - postmortem owner? devendra volunteered earlier. - checklist to include: kernel selection rules, quantization profile verification, kv cache eviction heuristics, canary traffic automation safety checks.

devendra: I can own postmortem. Will coordinate with jamie and chris.

alex: FYI alerted product on customer list; they might ping some OEMs. No escalations yet.

chris: quick note — logs showed model v13's forward pass had intermittent increase in memory working set around step 6 causing kernel fallback. We should add an instrumentation tag to metric 'kernel_fallback_rate' per model version.

lina: agree. I'll create a monitoring task and a Grafana panel for `kernel_fallback_rate{model=v*}`.

ingrid: closing loop for now. Current status: mitigated (reduced traffic + shard eviction) — keeping incident open for RCA. If anyone sees p99 > 900ms re-open and escalate to P1.

jamie: noted. thanks all. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and mitigation steps. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Notification: on-call handoff scheduled in 55 minutes to chris for overnight monitoring.

chris: I'll take handoff. Timestamps: initial alert 3699990001, mitigations at 3699990028-3699990040, stabilization confirmed at 3699990065.

devendra: attaching quick repro plan in ticket: steps, traces to capture, and suggested kernel pin.

lina: thanks — will follow up on dashboards tomorrow and add alert adjustment if kernel_fallback_rate rises for new canary rollouts.

ingrid: good work team. Keeping incident open for RCA.
